final_answer:
Let
\[
B_1=E_{12},\qquad B_2=E_{23},\qquad B_3=E_{31},
\]
so that
\[
A_i=-\alpha I+B_i.
\]
Since the scalar part commutes with everything and \(B_i^2=0\),
\[
e^{xA_1}=e^{-\alpha x}(I+xE_{12}),\quad
e^{yA_2}=e^{-\alpha y}(I+yE_{23}),\quad
e^{zA_3}=e^{-\alpha z}(I+zE_{31}).
\]
Thus the one-period monodromy matrix is
\[
P_{x,y,z}=e^{-\alpha}Q_{x,y,z},
\]
where
\[
Q_{x,y,z}=(I+zE_{31})(I+yE_{23})(I+xE_{12})
=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&x&xy\\
0&1&y\\
z&zx&1+xyz
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

So uniform exponential stability is possible exactly when
\[
e^{-\alpha}\sup_{x+y+z=1}\rho(Q_{x,y,z})<1.
\]

Now compute the characteristic polynomial of \(Q=Q_{x,y,z}\). Since \(\det Q=1\) and a direct determinant expansion gives
\[
\chi_Q(\lambda)
=\lambda^3-(3+xyz)\lambda^2+3\lambda-1
=(\lambda-1)^3-xyz\,\lambda^2.
\]
Let \(r=xyz\). By AM-GM,
\[
0\le r\le \frac1{27},
\]
with equality only at \(x=y=z=\frac13\).

For \(r>0\), the Perron root \(\lambda(r)>1\) satisfies
\[
(\lambda-1)^3=r\lambda^2.
\]
The function
\[
f(\lambda)=\frac{(\lambda-1)^3}{\lambda^2}
\]
is strictly increasing for \(\lambda>1\), since
\[
\frac{f'(\lambda)}{f(\lambda)}
=\frac{3}{\lambda-1}-\frac{2}{\lambda}
=\frac{\lambda+2}{\lambda(\lambda-1)}>0.
\]
Therefore \(\rho(Q_{x,y,z})\) is maximized when \(xyz\) is maximized, i.e. at
\[
x=y=z=\frac13.
\]

Let \(\lambda_*\) denote the unique real number \(>1\) satisfying
\[
27(\lambda_*-1)^3=\lambda_*^2.
\]
Equivalently, \(\lambda_*\) is the spectral radius of \(Q_{1/3,1/3,1/3}\). Hence
\[
\sup_{x+y+z=1}\rho(Q_{x,y,z})=\lambda_*.
\]

Thus the necessary and sufficient condition is
\[
e^{-\alpha}\lambda_*<1,
\]
or
\[
\alpha>\log\lambda_*.
\]

If \(\alpha\le \log\lambda_*\), taking \(x=y=z=\frac13\) gives a period map with spectral radius at least \(1\), so no uniform exponential decay can hold. If \(\alpha>\log\lambda_*\), all period maps have spectral radius uniformly \(<1\); compactness of the parameter simplex and boundedness of the within-period evolution then give constants \(M,\gamma>0\) independent of \((x,y,z)\).

Therefore the answer is
\[
\boxed{\left\{\alpha>0:\ \alpha>\log\lambda_*\right\}},
\]
where \(\lambda_*>1\) is the unique solution of
\[
\boxed{27(\lambda_*-1)^3=\lambda_*^2}.
\]
